CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows:
• Very strong C-H stretches at 2916 / 2862 cm⁻¹ without a 2960 cm⁻¹ band, indicating mainly CH₂ (no CH₃).  
• A moderately narrow band at 3309 cm⁻¹, consistent with an N-H stretch (primary amine) rather than the broader O-H stretch of alcohols.  
• CH₂ scissoring at 1446 cm⁻¹ and CH₂ twisting at 1289 cm⁻¹, both typical for cyclohexane derivatives.  
• Bands at 699–770 cm⁻¹ match ring-deformation modes reported for substituted cyclohexanes and include the ~700 cm⁻¹ NH₂ wag of primary amines.  
• A C–N stretch of a primary aliphatic amine is expected near 1040–1100 cm⁻¹; the 1091 cm⁻¹ band fits this.

Among the candidates, only 1–3 contain a primary amine and lack CH₃ groups. The 767/742 cm⁻¹ pattern and 1289 cm⁻¹ frequency best match six-membered cyclohexane ring modes rather than a seven-membered ring (candidate 2) or a ring bearing an extra –CH₂– substituent (candidate 3). Therefore, NC1CCCCCC1 (cyclohexylamine) is the most consistent with the observed Raman peaks.
